items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-09-30
items.q: He played with Louis one time. He was the same man Louis Armstrong was in one time in Chicago.

ctx.x: Now what about Johnny Sincere? Who did he play with?

He played with Louis one time. He was the same man Louis Armstrong was in one time in Chicago. Johnny was, Johnny Sincere. And he was very popular in the band. Johnny's quite a man. He's quite a band man, Johnny Sincere's, you know. He was quite a guitar. Of course his main way of making his living, I know you know that, but I tell you. The pleasure of living, you know. But he was quite an able man in the band, Johnny was, some years ago. Quite a guitar player.
Who did he play with down here? Do you remember?

items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-07-01
items.q: I got a record by them, with Louis on the cornet.

ctx.x: Well they had regular jazz music then. It was a jazz world and it was really a jazz music. The rest of the people copied from those bands then, you know, they picked it up from those bands. And so they had all the fellas, this is Dave, this is Oiskin Tate, was a very famous band playing at that time. You heard talk of him?
Sure. Did you? Teddy Weatherford? What? What I was saying. Wonderful piano player. I got a record by them, with Louis on the cornet.

Dave Payton, you heard Dave Payton. Joe Oliver used to play with him after Joe broke up his band. You heard of him in front of them. What the shit you said? Dave Payton and Oiskin Tate, he was director at the Vendome Theatre.
